results.fact: Number and length of the summit rappel
results.evidence: The archived 2004 report confirms a double-30 m rappel from a station on the ridge, but that party climbed the East Ridge to the Middle (main) summit from Sibley Pass, not the East Peak. A 2024 ascent from Hidden Lake says only that the party rappelled the fifth-class step, with no count or rope length. Still one East Peak account (two 30 m raps), so no patch.

results.evidence: The row describes the East (true) summit by the southeast shoulder from the Mineral Creek trailhead. Its only matching published figure is one report's 7.7 mi round trip (2,360-6,687 ft); a 2002 report used a spur-road start at 2,800 ft and gives no total, and the 10 mi / 4,600 ft figure belongs to a Middle Peak ascent by the south face. No second source for the East summit's one-way or round-trip distance, so dist_km, the summit waypoint and the 10 mi totalNote are not changed.

results.fact: dist_km (Approach one way) holds the round-trip figure
results.evidence: Decision rules 1 and 4: dist_km 30.58 km (19 mi), shown as 'Approach (one way)', equals the itinerary's round-trip total and is provably not a one-way figure. The Park Service gives Cascade Pass at 3.7 mi from the trailhead with Pelton Basin camps just below it on the Stehekin side, and a trail listing gives the Pelton Basin camp as an 8.82 mi out-and-back; the route leaves the trail at Pelton Basin, and the row's own waypoints put the summit at 9.5 mi. No source states the one-way distance to the summit, so the value is cleared rather than replaced.

results.fact: Whether the route tops out on Trapper Mountain's summit
results.evidence: No new first-hand account found; the known reports (2012 first ski descent, 2024 car-to-car) and a note on a 1970s ascent say only that parties topped out the couloir. Nothing states whether the route continues to the 7,530 ft summit, so high_point_ft and the summit waypoint are left as they are.

Sources give only car-to-car gain (6,115 and 6,085 ft, matching gain_ft 6,100); none states a loss figure. Writing loss_ft = gain_ft on an out-and-back is the refused loss_ft class, and no stated loss exists to replace 800, so it stays flagged.
